Lemma
[Dirichlet a priori $W^{2,p}$ estimate] 1. ch9:9.17\group chapter-9Source: gilbarg-trudinger:page-0254 Under the hypotheses of Theorem 40, there is a constant $C$, independent of $u$, such that \begin{equation} \tag {9.46} \| u\| _{2,p;\Omega }\le C\| Lu\| _{p;\Omega } \end{equation} for every $u\in W^{2,p}(\Omega )\cap W^{1,p}_0(\Omega )$.
Proof

\sketch Otherwise normalize a sequence by $\| u_m\| _p=1$ while $\| Lu_m\| _p\to 0$. The boundary estimate gives a uniform $W^{2,p}$ bound. Compactness in $L^p$ and weak compactness in $W^{2,p}$ produce a nonzero limit $u$ with $Lu=0$ and zero trace, contradicting uniqueness.

□
